 Alex Cora's run with the Red Sox came to an end when the club parted ways with the longtime manager in April. Despite the abrupt exit early in the 2026 season, Boston will always be a special place for Cora and his family.
 During an interview with Rob Bradford on the "Baseball Isn't Boring" podcast , Cora shared a touching story about one of his twin boys seeing Fenway Park after Cora had left the team. Cora's family was traveling to a World Cup viewing party at City Hall Plaza, and his son had an emotional reaction as the car passed Fenway Park.
 "All of a sudden, it's very quiet, right? And we look back, and one of the boys was crying," Cora told Bradford. "And [Cora's fiancee] Angelica turns around, and he tries to hide. And she's like, 'No, no, no, no, no, you cry because we lived here for six, seven years. This is part of our life. And we will always remember Fenway. We will always love the Red Sox.'"
 The Alex Cora @BBisntBoring conversation drops at midnight tonight. Spoiler: It's a long one because there was a lot to talk about. https://t.co/49kr9xIpOH
— Rob Bradford (@bradfo) October 25, 2026 Cora left the dugout after the Red Sox lost 17 of their first 27 games, dropping them to last place in the American League East standings. He finished with an overall record of 620-541 in Boston, and he led the team to a championship in 2018.
 While Cora enjoyed spending time with his family this past summer, he did follow the Red Sox's impressive turnaround under new manager Chad Tracy — and his kids were still cheering for them.
 "The Red Sox were playing the Tigers, and I'm watching the beginning of it," Cora said. "And one of the boys comes down, and he's like, 'Who's playing?' I'm like, 'Tigers and Red Sox.' And he goes, 'Who are we pulling for?' I'm like, 'Who do you want to win? Which team do you want to win?'
 "And he goes, 'The Red Sox, of course.'"
